findings: Re-pin timing is ambiguous: section 5 says the Locksmith 'may not re-pin after... the opening Probe,' but section 4's turn structure lists the re-pin window as available after ANY failed Probe with no first-turn exception. A reader following only section 4 would think re-pin is legal after the round's very first failed Probe. The worked example (turn 1 is a failed Probe, no re-pin follows) shows 'opening Probe' means 'the round's first Probe,' but that reading only surfaces by cross-checking the example against two separate sections, not from either section's prose alone.

The worked scoring example has an internal arithmetic mismatch. The recap states 'six failed turns paid 6, two re-pins cost 4' (which nets to 2), but the turn table shows 7 income-paying turns before the open (6 failed Probes plus 1 Hold, since section 4 step 3 says Holds pay the Locksmith too) minus 4 for two re-pins, netting the stated final score of 3. The prose undercounts by one because it omits the Hold's contribution to the tally, so a reader trying to verify the math from the summary sentence alone gets the wrong number.
